title: From models to materials
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: S2.4#c11 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S2.4#c12 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S2.4#c09 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S2.4#c01 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. Questions: S2.4#q01, S2.4#q03, S2.4#q06, S2.4#q09, S2.4#q12, S2.4#q02, S2.4#q04, S2.4#q07, S2.4#q10, S2.4#q13, S2.4#q08, S2.4#q11, S2.4#q14, S2.4#q15, S2.4#q16, S2.4#q17.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Polymer (macromolecule)
items.clue: A very large chain of many repeating subunits joined by covalent bonds.

items.label: Monomer
items.clue: A small molecule that can join repeatedly with others to form a long chain.

items.label: Alloy
items.clue: A mixture of a metal with other metals or non-metals, with no fixed formula.

items.label: Bonding continuum
items.clue: The idea that ionic, covalent and metallic are ends of a range, not separate boxes.

questions.stem: Using the electronegativities Na 0.9, Mg 1.3, Al 1.6, Si 1.9, P 2.2 and Cl 3.2, the electronegativity differences for NaCl, MgCl₂, AlCl₃, SiCl₄ and PCl₃ are 2.3, 1.9, 1.6, 1.3 and 1.0. Which statement about the bonding in this series is correct?

options.text: The bonds are ionic up to AlCl₃ and covalent from SiCl₄ on, where the metals end.
Ionic character decreases and covalent character increases gradually along the series.
Ionic character increases along the series, as the average electronegativity rises.
In SiCl₄ some of the Si–Cl bonds are ionic and the others are fully covalent.

questions.stem: The position of a binary compound in the bonding triangle is found from the electronegativities of its two elements. In the triangle the metallic vertex is at the bottom left, the covalent vertex at the bottom right and the ionic vertex at the top; the two bottom vertices are elements, for which Δχ = 0. For aluminium chloride, AlCl₃, χ(Al) = 1.6 and χ(Cl) = 3.2. What is the x-coordinate of AlCl₃ in the bonding triangle?
Which description of an alloy is correct?

options.text: A compound of a metal with other elements, bonded in a fixed ratio by formula
A mixture of a metal with other metals or non-metals, in variable amounts
A mixture of two or more metals, with no atoms of a non-metal present in it
A mixture of a metal with another element, made so that it is softer

questions.explanation: An alloy is a mixture, so its composition can vary, and the added element can be a metal (zinc in brass) or a non-metal (carbon in steel). Alloys usually have enhanced properties, such as greater hardness.

questions.stem: Which statement about polymers is correct?

options.text: Polymers are synthetic plastics; substances made by living things are not.
Fats are natural polymers made of many glycerol and fatty acid units.
Glucose is a natural polymer, as it is the building block of starch and cellulose.
Cellulose (natural) and nylon (synthetic) are both polymers built from monomers.

questions.explanation: Cellulose is a natural polymer of glucose, made by plants; nylon is a synthetic polyamide made industrially. Both are macromolecules built from many repeating monomer units, so being a polymer does not depend on being natural or synthetic.

questions.stem: Propene, CH₂=CHCH₃, forms the addition polymer poly(propene), written as [repeating unit]ₙ. Which option gives the repeating unit and describes it correctly?

options.text: –CH₂=CH(CH₃)–, keeping each monomer's C=C
–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–, one unit of a single long chain
–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–, all three carbons in the main chain
CH₃CH₂CH₃, one of n separate small molecules

questions.explanation: One bond of each C=C breaks and the two former C=C carbons form the main chain, with CH₃ as a side group. The formula [–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–]ₙ represents one chain molecule containing n of these units.

questions.stem: Magnesium oxide (χ: Mg 1.3, O 3.4; Δχ = 2.1) lies high in the bonding triangle, towards the ionic vertex. Solid magnesium oxide does not conduct electricity, but molten magnesium oxide does. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Melting splits its MgO molecules into separate ions, which then carry the current.
Its ions become liquid when it melts, and liquid ions can carry charge but solid ones cannot.
Its ions cannot move in the solid, but in the melt they move and carry the current.
Melting sets electrons free, which then move through the liquid and carry the current.

questions.stem: With χ(Sn) = 2.0 and χ(Cl) = 3.2, tin(IV) chloride, SnCl₄, has an electronegativity difference of 1.2 and an average electronegativity of 2.6. Sodium chloride has an electronegativity difference of 2.3. Which prediction about SnCl₄ is correct?

options.text: It has a low boiling point, as its molecules are held by weak intermolecular forces.
It has a high melting point, as a metal chloride is a lattice of metal and chloride ions.
Its vapour consists of separate Sn and Cl atoms, as boiling must break its Sn–Cl bonds.
It conducts electricity when solid, as it contains atoms of the metal tin.

questions.stem: A bronze used for springs and bearings is an alloy of copper containing about 5% tin. Tin atoms are larger than copper atoms, and pure tin is a soft metal. Which statement comparing this bronze with pure copper is correct?

options.text: Bronze is harder, as the larger tin atoms disrupt the layers of copper atoms.
Bronze is softer, as a mixture of metals is weaker than a pure metal.
Bronze is softer, as its tin atoms are themselves soft and pass this on to the alloy.
Bronze is harder, as copper and tin form a compound with a fixed formula.

questions.explanation: In pure copper the layers of identical cations slide over each other easily. The larger tin atoms distort the regular layers, so the layers cannot slide as easily and bronze is harder. The non-directional metallic bonding holds the tin atoms in the lattice, so bronze remains a metal.

questions.stem: Poly(ethene) is a plastic that softens when heated and can then be moulded into a new shape. What happens in the plastic as it softens?

options.text: The chains gain enough energy to overcome the forces between them and slide past each other.
Heat flows into the gaps between the chains as a substance and pushes the chains apart.
The covalent bonds between neighbouring chains break, so the chains separate.
Each chain molecule itself becomes soft, so the plastic as a whole softens.

questions.explanation: Poly(ethene) consists of long chains held together only by intermolecular (London) forces. Heating gives the chains enough energy to overcome these forces partly, so they slide past each other and the plastic can be reshaped. The covalent bonds in the chains are not broken.

questions.stem: A section of an addition polymer is –CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–. Which is the monomer?

options.text: (CH₃)₃CH
CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃
(CH₃)₃COH
(CH₃)₂C=CH₂

questions.explanation: The repeating unit is –CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–: a two-carbon unit of the main chain with two CH₃ side groups on one carbon. Restoring the C=C between the two main-chain carbons gives (CH₃)₂C=CH₂. The monomer has exactly the same atoms as the repeating unit.

questions.stem: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc. Like copper, brass conducts electricity and can be hammered into shape. Which statement about the bonding in brass is correct?

options.text: Copper and zinc atoms bond in a fixed ratio, as they would in a compound of the two.
Covalent bonds join the atoms, as metallic bonding needs atoms of a single element.
Delocalized electrons hold all the cations, as the bonding is non-directional.
Zinc atoms give electrons to copper atoms, so that ionic bonds form between them.

questions.explanation: Brass is held by metallic bonding, which is non-directional: the delocalized electrons attract every cation, whatever its element. So zinc atoms fit into the lattice, the delocalized electrons carry current, and layers can be moved without breaking the bonding.

questions.stem: Which property of poly(ethene) is correctly explained in terms of its structure?

options.text: It is an electrical insulator, as it contains no metal atoms to carry a current.
It softens on heating, as the covalent bonds in its chains break apart.
It is an electrical insulator, as all of its valence electrons are in localized bonds.
It does not biodegrade, as synthetic substances cannot be broken down by organisms.

questions.explanation: Poly(ethene) consists of chains of C–C and C–H covalent bonds. Every valence electron is held in a bond between two particular atoms, and there are no ions, so there are no mobile charged particles to carry a current.

questions.stem: A polyamide forms from ethane-1,2-diamine, H₂N(CH₂)₂NH₂ (M_r = 60.12), and butanedioyl dichloride, ClOC(CH₂)₂COCl (M_r = 154.98). Using A_r values H 1.01, C 12.01, N 14.01, O 16.00 and Cl 35.45, what is the M_r of one repeating unit of the polymer?
questions.explanation: Each repeating unit contains one residue of each monomer, and two amide links form per unit, each releasing HCl: 60.12 + 154.98 − 2 × 36.46 = 142.18. The repeating unit is –NH(CH₂)₂NHCO(CH₂)₂CO–, C₆H₁₀N₂O₂.

questions.stem: Ethane-1,2-diol, HOCH₂CH₂OH, and hexanedioic acid, HOOC(CH₂)₄COOH, react to form a polyester. Which option gives the repeating unit and describes it correctly?

options.text: –OCH₂CH₂OOC(CH₂)₄CO–, with two H₂O lost per unit
–OCH₂CH₂OOC(CH₂)₄COOH, with one H₂O lost per unit
–O(H)CH₂CH₂O(H)C(O)(OH)(CH₂)₄C(O)(OH)–, with no atoms lost
–OCH₂CH₂O–, with each unit made from a single monomer

questions.stem: Which statement about biological macromolecules is correct?

options.text: Starch forms from glucose by hydrolysis, with a water molecule released at each link.
Proteins are hydrolyzed to amino acids, with water used to break each amide link.
DNA is hydrolyzed simply as it dissolves in water, without any covalent bonds breaking.
Cellulose forms from glucose by addition, with no atoms at all lost from the monomers.

questions.explanation: All biological macromolecules form by condensation and are broken down by hydrolysis. In the hydrolysis of a protein, one water molecule reacts with each amide (peptide) link, giving the amino acids.

questions.stem: Hexane-1,6-diamine, H₂N(CH₂)₆NH₂, and decanedioic acid, HOOC(CH₂)₈COOH, react to form the polyamide nylon-6,10. Which option gives the repeating unit and describes it correctly?

options.text: –NH(CH₂)₆NHCO(CH₂)₈CO–, with two H₂O lost per unit
–NH(CH₂)₆NHCO(CH₂)₈COOH, with one H₂O lost per unit
–NH₂(CH₂)₆NH₂C(O)(OH)(CH₂)₈C(O)(OH)–, with no atoms lost
–NH(CH₂)₆NH–, with a single monomer in each unit

questions.explanation: Each –NH₂ of the diamine reacts with a –COOH of the acid to form an amide link, –CONH–, releasing H₂O. The repeating unit contains one residue of each monomer: each N has lost one H and each C=O carbon its –OH, with two amide links (two H₂O) per unit, giving C₁₆H₃₀N₂O₂.
